pages.text: Tomorrow was Mom's birthday. One white daisy always sat in her apron pocket.
"I want to give Mom flowers," Mumu whispered.
Dodo puffed out her chest. "I know Mom's favorite! The biggest yellow sunflower!"
They went to the field. Sunflowers were much, much taller than Dodo.
Dodo hugged a stalk and pulled hard. It didn't budge.
Thump! She landed on her bottom. The sunflower stood straight and looked down at her.
"This flower... is stronger than Mom." Dodo looked up.
Mumu picked a handful of white daisies by the stream, the very flowers from Mom's apron.
The next morning, Mumu offered the daisies. "Happy birthday, Mom!" She smiled wide and buried her nose in them to sniff.
Just then, Dodo and Dad struggled outside the door. The sunflower Dad had cut was bigger than the doorway! Mom put it in a jar beside the door. The flower guard nodded in the wind.
